title: Hungary – Construction work – CT/MR kivitelezés
description: Dinamikus beszerzési rendszer létrehozása, amelynek tárgya CT és MR berendezések kivitelezési munkáinak beszerzése dinamikus beszerzési rendszer keretében Ajánlatkérő részére. A DBR fennállásának időtartama (48 hónap) alatt megrendelni kívánt teljes mennyiség becsült nagyságrendje: CT telepítéséhez kapcsolódó kivitelezési feladat tervezetten 77db MR telepítéséhez kapcsolódó kivitelezési feladat tervezetten 38 db összesen: tervezetten 115 darab Tervezett feladatok felsorolása: A vonatkozó jogszabályokban rögzített kivitelezői és felelős műszaki vezetői feladatok (191/2009. (IX. 15.) Korm. rendelet 12–14. §) és az egyedi ajánlattételi felhívásban és szerződésben meghatározott követelmények szerint különösen: • A munkákkal és a szállítási útvonalakkal érintett épületrészek, közművek és környező területek állapotfelvételi dokumentációjának elkészítése. • Az Intézmény ellátásszervezési rendjéhez és a betegellátás folyamatosságához igazodó részletes térbeli és időbeli kivitelezési organizációs terv készítése (különösen a felvonulási és raktározási területek, a munkavégzési idők, a zaj- és porterhelés csökkentését szolgáló intézkedések, a személyek és gépjárművek be- és kiléptetése, az épületen belüli mozgás és anyagszállítás, valamint a beteg-, személyzeti és mentőforgalom, továbbá a menekülési útvonalak fenntartásának szabályozásával), egyeztetése és jóváhagyásra benyújtása. • Részletes ütemterv készítése, egyeztetése az Intézménnyel, a Műszaki üzemeltetővel és az Eszközbeszállítóval, valamint jóváhagyásra benyújtása a munkaterület átvételét megelőzően. Az ütemtervnek pontosan tartalmaznia kell a közműkizárások, rendszerleállások és területlezárások kezdési és befejezési időpontját, valamint időtartamát; a CT/MR berendezések beszállításához és telepítéséhez igazított készültségi fokokat és azok elérésének határidőit; továbbá a betegellátást és annak folyamatosságát befolyásoló valamennyi építési-szerelési fázist és ezek időbeli összehangolását. Az egyeztetések lefolytatásáért, az érintett szereplők ellátásszervezési, üzemeltetési és eszköztelepítési követelményeinek ütemtervbe történő beépítéséért, valamint az ütemterv megvalósíthatóságáért és folyamatos aktualizálásáért, továbbá a kritikus úton lévő építési termékek határidőben történő beszerzéséért a Kivitelező felel. • A kivitelezés előkészítése és teljes időtartama során folyamatos egyeztetés az Intézménnyel és a Műszaki üzemeltetővel, a betegellátás folyamatosságának biztosítása, az ellátásszervezési követelmények és az intézményi működésből eredő kötöttségek figyelembevétele érdekében. Tervezett munkanemek felsorolása: A meglévő helyiségek és beszállítási útvonalak építészeti átalakítása; diagnosztikai berendezések fogadásához szükséges építési munkák és árnyékolások; komplex épületgépészeti rendszerek kivitelezése, így légtechnikai, hűtési-fűtési, szükség szerinti páratartalom-szabályozási, vízellátási és csatornázási munkák; komplex erősáramú energiaellátási rendszerek kivitelezése, beleértve a betáplálás, elosztás, kábelezés, védelem, földelés és EPH (egyenpotenciálra hozó, potenciálkiegyenlítő rendszer) kialakítását; a kapcsolódó gyengeáramú, tűzjelző és informatikai rendszerek szerelése, valamint a szükséges mérések, beszabályozások és próbaüzemek. A pontos tartalmat helyszínenként a terv határozza meg. A 321/2015 (X.30.) Korm. rendelet 46. § (3)-(5) bekezdésére figyelemmel ajánlatkérő felhívja a figyelmet, hogy, amennyiben a közbeszerzés tárgyának egyértelmű és közérthető meghatározása szükségessé tette meghatározott gyártmányú vagy eredetű dologra, illetve konkrét eljárásra, amely egy adott gazdasági szereplő termékeit vagy az általa nyújtott szolgáltatásokat jellemzi, vagy védjegyre, szabadalomra, tevékenységre, személyre, típusra vagy adott származásra vagy gyártási folyamatra való hivatkozást, a megnevezés csak a tárgy jellegének egyértelmű meghatározása érdekében történt, és megnevezés mellett a „vagy azzal egyenértékű” minden esetben értendő. Egyenértékű dolog megajánlása esetén az egyenértékűséget az ajánlattevőnek az ajánlatában igazolnia kell.

title: CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES, WHITEHORSE CADET TRAINING CENTRE WHITEHORSE
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Construction Management Services, Whitehorse cadet training centre whitehorse, yukon (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Whitehorse, Yukon. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES The objective of this contract is to recapitalize both vertical and horizontal infrastructure at the Whitehorse Cadet Training Centre (WCTC) through a multi-year program. The existing WCTC site includes a diverse portfolio of facilities comprising 39 buildings with a total floor area of approximately 5,000 m². These facilities include barracks with associated ablution areas, classrooms, a combined kitchen/dining/administration building, a large storage warehouse, and various workshops and auxiliary support structures. The recapitalization program will encompass the renovation of existing buildings, as well as the demolition and reconstruction of selected facilities, to modernize and enhance the overall functionality of the site. Project delivery will be undertaken using a Construction Management (CM) contract. The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project. To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the CM contract. The IBPs will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities. It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN: APN_NPYKCM01 Approximate Estimate: $50M Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent  will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS) 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors  that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors  that do not submit a proposal  will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. description: Hankinta jaetaan kahteen osakokonaisuuteen siten, että ensimmäinen osakokonaisuus on suur- ja keskijännitejohtojen pohjanraivaus, pienjännitejohtojen raivaus, reunapuiden oksiminen ja kaato, raivausrisujen kerääminen ja kuljettaminen, muut raivaus- ja tarkastustyöt sekä sähkönjakeluverkkojen läheisyydessä annettava puunkaatoapu. Tilaaja valitsee 1-2 tarjoajaa toimittajakseen tähän osakokonaisuuteen. Toinen osakokonaisuus on puunkaatoaputilausten vastaanottopalvelu. Tilaaja valitsee yhden tarjoajan toimittajakseen tähän osakokonaisuuteen. Ensimmäiseen osakokonaisuuteen tarjoavien Tarjoajien on osallistuttava Tilaajan pyytäessä varallaoloon, jonka tarkoituksena valmistautua raivaamaan kaatuneita tai kallistuneita puita johtojen läheisyydessä myrskyn aikana tai myrskyn jälkeen. Osatarjoukset hyväksytään siten, että tarjoaja voi tarjota yhteen tai useampaan osakokonaisuuteen., Raivaus- ja puunkaatoapupalvelut Osakokonaisuus sisältää seuraavat palvelut: - suurjännitejohtoalueiden (110 kV) pohjan raivaus - keskijännitejohtoalueiden (20 kV) pohjan raivaus - avojohtimisten pienjännitejohtoalueiden (0,4 kV) raivaus - riippukierrejohtimisten (AMKA) pienjännitejohtoalueiden (0,4 kV) raivaus - keskijännitejohtoalueiden (20 kV) reunapuiden oksiminen - reunapuiden kaato pien- ja keskijännitejohtoalueiden vieressä - raivausrisujen kerääminen ja kuljettaminen keräyspisteeseen - muut erikseen sovittavat raivaustyöt tai raivaustarpeen tarkastustyöt - Tarjoajan käytössä olevan työkaluston käyttäminen muissa töissä - puhelimitse annettava puunkaadon neuvonta ja kaatoluvan antaminen - paikan päällä annettava puunkaadon neuvonta ja avustus - raivauksen varallaolo myrskyn uhatessa Pohjan raivauksella tarkoitetaan johtoalueen pohjan raivausta siten, että johtoalueella voi raivauksen jälkeen liikkua moottorikelkalla, mönkijällä tai jalan. Tämä edellyttää, että raivauksen jälkeen johtoalueella ei ole yli 10 cm korkeita kantoja ja että kantojen leikkauspinta on suora. Pohjan raivaus tehdään joko raivaussahoilla tai vaihtoehtoisesti koneellisesti. Pohjan raivauksen yhteydessä poistetaan yksittäiset johtokadun ulkopuolella kasvavat puut, joiden riski kaatua johdon päälle on merkittävä. Reunapuiden oksimisella tarkoitetaan johtoalueen reunalla kasvavien puiden oksien katkaisemista siten, että oksat eivät ulotu johtoalueelle. Oksinta on tehtävä niin, ettei kasvavia puita tarpeettomasti vaurioiteta. Johtoalueen leveys vaihtelee johtotyypin mukaan. Tarjouspyynnön liitteistä käyvät ilmi johtokadun leveysvaatimukset eri johtotyypeille. Raivausrisujen keräämisellä ja kuljettamisella keräyspisteeseen tarkoitetaan oksien yms. raivausjätteen viemistä ennalta sovittuun paikkaan. Keskimääräinen kuljetusmatka sopimus- ja optiokaudella raivattavista kohteista keräyspisteeseen on noin 10 km. Jos Tarjoajalla on käytettävissään työkalustoa, jota Tilaaja voi käyttää myös muissa kuin tässä tarjouspyynnössä mainituissa töissä, Tarjoaja voi tarjota työkalustoa Tilaajaan käyttöön yksilöimällä työkaluston yksikköhintaluettelossa ja määrittämällä työkalustolle yksikköhinnan. Tarjoaja voi valita käytettävän yksikön yksikköhinnalle. Raivaustöiden tilaus tapahtuu sähköisillä työmääräyksillä. Tarjoaja dokumentoi tehdyt raivaustyöt Tilaajan tietojärjestelmään saman vuorokauden kuluessa tehdystä työstä. Tilaaja antaa tarvittavat käyttöoikeudet ja perehdytyksen käytettäviin tietojärjestelmiin. Tarjoaja vastaa tarvittavasta luvituksesta johtokadun ulkopuolelta kaadettavien puiden osalta. Pyydettäessä Tilaaja kytkee raivattavat johto-osuudet jännitteettömäksi, jos raivaustyön turvallisuus tätä vaatii. Puunkaatoapupalveluun sisältyy Tilaajan asiakkaille annettava neuvonta ja puunkaatoapu tapauksissa, joissa puun kaataminen voi aiheuttaa jännitteisen sähkönjakeluverkon vuoksi vaaraa puun kaatajalle tai jossa puun kaataminen voi vaurioittaa sähköverkkoa. Keskijännitejohtojen läheisyydessä olevien puiden kaatoneuvonta ja avustus tapahtuu aina paikan päällä. Palveluun sisältyy ohjeistus puun turvalliseen kaatoon. Puun kaataminen ei sisälly neuvontapalveluun. Pienjännitejohtojen läheisyydessä olevien puiden kaato-ohjeet sekä ohjeet sähköturvallisuuden varmistamisesta annetaan puhelimitse ja samalla annetaan kaatolupa asiakkaan hankkimalle ammattitaitoiselle metsurille. Mikäli puhelinneuvonta ei riitä, voidaan puunkaatoneuvontaa antaa paikan päällä. Puunkaatoapupalveluun ei sisälly itse puun kaataminen, pois lukien sellaiset erityistilanteet, joissa puun kaatuminen uhkaa ainoastaan Tilaajan sähkönjakeluverkkoa. Näissä tilanteissa puunkaato on Tilaajan asiakkaalle maksutonta. Tarjoajan on kyettävä toimittamaan puhelimitse annettavaa puunkaatoneuvontaa kahden arkipäivän kuluessa asiakkaan tekemästä tilauksesta sekä paikan päällä annettavaa kaatoneuvontaa ja/tai kaadon avustusta vähintään kymmenen arkipäivän kuluessa tilauksesta. Tarjoajaa pyydetään selvittämään, miten Tarjoaja kykenee vastaamaan palvelutarpeeseen tarjoamallaan toimitusajalla. Puunkaatoapupalvelussa Tilaaja on antanut asiakaslupauksen, jossa puunkaadon neuvontapalvelua annetaan kahden arkipäivän ja paikan päällä asiakkaan kohteessa kymmenen arkipäivän kuluessa. Mikäli Toimittaja ei toimita tilattua palvelua sovitussa ajassa, on Toimittaja velvollinen maksamaan Tilaajalle sopimussakkoa 500 euroa myöhästynyttä tilausta kohden. Raivauksen varallaololla myrskyn uhatessa tarkoitetaan toimintaa, jossa Tilaaja pyytää Toimittajaa varautumaan raivaustöihin tulevan myrskyn aiheuttaman mahdollisen raivaustarpeen seurauksena. Tilaaja ja Toimittaja sopivat erikseen varallaolon laajuudesta ja tasosta. Varallaolo alkaa, kun Tilaaja tilaa varallaolon, ja päättyy, kun Tilaaja ilmoittaa Toimittajalle varallaolon päättyneen. Yksikköhinnalla tarkoitetaan yhden henkilön varallaolon hintaa. Varallaolon aikana varalla olevien henkilöiden on oltava Tilaajan käytettävissä sovittuna aikana siitä, kun Tilaaja on ilmoittanut tarpeen henkilön käyttöön. Varallaoloaikana tehdystä työstä veloitetaan sovittujen yksikköhintojen mukaisesti. Toimittaja vastaa siitä, että sillä on käytettävissä vähintään X henkilöä raivaustöiden suorittamiseen ja varallaoloon myrskyn uhatessa. Toimittajan varallaolossa olevan henkilöstö on Tilaajan käytettävissä X minuutin sisällä myrskyvarallaolon aikana. Mikäli Toimittaja ei pysty asettamaan Tilaajan käyttöön sovitussa ajassa sovittua määrää henkilöstöä, on Toimittaja velvollinen maksamaan Tilaajalle sopimussakkoa 3000 €/puuttuva henkilö/varallaolo., Puunkaatoaputilausten vastaanotto Puunkaatoaputilausten vastaanotto sisältää - puhelimitse tulevien puunkaatoaputilausten sekä -ilmoitusten sähköjohdolle vaaraa aiheuttavista puista vastaanottamisen - tilausten kirjaamisen Tilaajan tietojärjestelmään. Puunkaatoaputilausten puheluiden vastaanottopalvelun on oltava Tilaajan asiakkaiden saatavissa arkisin klo 8-16 välisenä aikana. Tilaukset on kirjattava samassa yhteydessä Tilaajan tietojärjestelmään. Tarjoajan tulee esittää selvitys, miten tilausten vastaanottopalvelu järjestetään.,

Hankinnasta tehdään puitesopimus vuosien 2027-2031 ajaksi. Varsinainen sopimuskausi 2027-2029 sekä yksi kahden vuoden optiokausi. title: Floor Refinishing Services
description: The U.S. Coast Guard Academy, New London, Connecticut, intends to procure hardwood basketball court floor refinishing services. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, transportation, and incidental services necessary to perform annual screen-and-recoat maintenance for the approximately 17,422-square-foot Roland Hall Gymnasium court and, when included and funded, biennial services for the approximately 12,129-square-foot Billard Hall Gymnasium court. Services include cleaning, mechanically screening or abrading the existing finish as necessary, removing dust and debris, and applying an approved high-solids, low-VOC, oil-based commercial athletic-floor finish compatible with the existing coating system. Base CLIN services are limited to screen-and-recoat maintenance and do not include sanding to bare wood, repainting or restoration of court markings unless damaged by the Contractor or repairs other than repairs necessary to correct Contractor-caused damage. The requirement also includes an optional, firm-fixed-price per-square-foot CLIN for full refinishing of additional Government hardwood-floor areas, if authorized. The contractor shall protect existing court markings and Government property, comply with applicable safety and environmental requirements, coordinate the work schedule with the Contracting Officer�s Representative, and return each court to a clean, safe, uniform, and playable condition.

title: Phase 1 - Warden Building Reno Concept Design, Banff National Park
description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS TO BIDDERS (SI) This is a two stage selection process. Proponents responding to this selection process are requested to submit a proposal in two stages. This posting is the first stage (Stage One) of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage will evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers; the second stage (Stage Two) will invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial proposal on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Upon award of contract in Stage Two the pre-qualification list will expire and will not be used in any other solicitation. The qualification list will expire within 180 days or upon award of a contract in Stage Two, whichever is earlier, and the prequalification list will not be used in any other solicitation. Following the evaluation of the submissions of Stage One, proponents will be advised of their qualification result and the status of the tender. Parks Canada reserves the right to re-issue Stage One via a /B solicitation if it is determined there is insufficient competition to proceed with Stage Two. Proponents that have qualified in Stage One /A will not be required to resubmit on the Stage One /B. Proponents that failed to demonstrate compliance on the Stage One /A may resubmit and will be considered in Stage One. Stage Two Proponents will be provided a REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) for further qualifications and the financial evaluation in relation to the specifications and drawings. LIST OF PRE-QUALIFIED BIDDERS: A list of pre-qualified bidders from Stage One will not be released. Contract award notice of the successful bidder of Stage Two will be posted on http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities PARTNER WITH ANOTHER BUSINESS: Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business” REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) is planning the rehabilitation of an existing approximately 65,000 sq. ft. multi-purpose facility that will serve as a centralized operations hub in Banff National Park, Alberta. The building will accommodate a combination of administrative office functions, light industrial storage areas, and specialized trades workspaces to support current and future operational requirements. To support this initiative, PCA is seeking to retain an Architectural Consultant to provide comprehensive architectural and planning services through the conceptual design phase. The Consultant will develop and present three (3) distinct conceptual design options for stakeholder review, evaluation, and selection, supported by functional planning, site analysis, and preliminary cost and schedule considerations. In addition, the Consultant will be required to complete an analysis of project delivery methods. It is the expectation that the Consultant will provide a recommended option and preferred delivery model for the project. Multiple technical assessments have been completed to evaluate the existing condition of the facility, including the building envelope, structural systems, mechanical systems, electrical systems, and fire and life safety components. In addition, an energy audit has been conducted to identify opportunities for improved building performance and energy efficiency. A summary of these detailed findings will be provided during Phase 2 of the tender. The Consultant will be expected to undertake a thorough review of the available information, validate key findings and assumptions, and refine recommendations as necessary to support the eventual development of the conceptual design options. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE The consultant must perform and complete the services described in the project statement by September 30, 2027. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Fire Alarm System Inspection and Maintenance, various locations Alberta
description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) requires Fire Alarm System Inspection and Maintenance Services for multiple Detachment locations within Alberta. The contract period will be for three years (one year, with the option to extended for 2 additional one-year periods) from the date of contract. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation of bids is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. This is an open tender. However, it will be conditionally set-aside under the Government of Canada’s Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) if two or more bids have been received by Indigenous businesses who are certified under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) criteria and who may be listed in the Government of Canada’s Indigenous Business Directory (https://www.sac-isc.gc.ca/eng/1100100033057/1610797769658). If your Indigenous business is not yet registered in the Indigenous Business Directory, please do so at the link provided above. If bids from two or more Indigenous businesses are compliant with the terms of the Request for Proposal, the contracting authority will limit the competition to those Indigenous businesses and will not consider bids from any non-Indigenous businesses that may have been submitted. If the bids from the Indigenous businesses are found to be non-compliant or non-responsive or are withdrawn, such that fewer than two compliant bids from Indigenous businesses remain, bids from all of the non-Indigenous businesses that had submitted bids will then be considered by the contracting authority. Security: This solicitation contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory technical criteria to be declared responsive. The responsive bid with the lowest evaluated price will be recommended for award of a contract. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit as per page one of the Request for Proposal (RFP). Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. The RCMP has adopted the Ineligibility and Suspension Policy administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada. As a result, the supplier integrity and compliance provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. Indigenous Procurement: The federal Indigenous Business Directory (IBD) is an online resource for all levels of government and the private sector to identify Indigenous business capacity. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. A profile in the IBD can also allow you to compete for federal government contracts that are set-aside for Indigenous businesses through the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses. For more information and to review eligibility criteria and register, visit: www.canada.ca/indigenousbusinessdirectory.

title: Installation of piping for wastewater, drainage, and sewerage at Geological Survey of Canada - Calgary (GSCC)
description: 3.1.1 The work covered by this service contract includes, but is not limited to, the provision of skilled labour, tools, and materials required to perform a wide range of tasks associated with wastewater, drainage, and sewerage piping systems throughout the facility. This includes installation, modification, replacement, testing, and commissioning of piping systems and associated components. 3.1.2 Services include site preparation; removal and disposal of existing piping, including the safe abatement and handling of asbestos-containing materials in accordance with all applicable regulations and approved procedures; installation of new piping systems; connection to existing infrastructure; and verification of proper system operation through inspection and testing. 3.1.3 The work also includes troubleshooting and repair of existing systems; ensuring proper flow, drainage, and system integrity; and confirming compliance with applicable codes, standards, and environmental regulations. All asbestos abatement activities must be carried out by qualified personnel following regulatory requirements and safety protocols. 3.1.4 The Contractor shall ensure that all work is performed with minimal disruption to facility operations and in coordination with NRCan’s facility management team. Documentation of completed work must be provided, including detailed descriptions of services performed, materials used, test results, identified deficiencies, and recommendations for corrective actions, system improvements, or preventative maintenance. 3.1.5 The installation of new roof drain piping, sewerage piping, and chemical-resistant laboratory piping includes labour, materials, fittings, valves, supports, hangers, anchors, penetrations, connections, testing, inspections, commissioning, restoration of affected surfaces, waste removal, and all other incidentals required to provide a complete and fully operational system.

title: Germany – Restaurant and food-serving services – Gastronomische Bewirtschaftung der Stadthalle Magdeburg
description: Die Messe und Veranstaltungsgesellschaft Magdeburg GmbH ist eine Beteiligungs-gesellschaft der Stadt Magdeburg, welche ihr die Nutzungsrechte der Stadthalle in Magdeburg vertraglich übertragen hat. Sie führt in diesem Objekt Veranstaltungen durch und vermietet es an Gastveranstalter zur Durchführung von Veranstaltungen aller Art. In dieser Eigenschaft ist die Betriebsführungsgesellschaft MVGM durch die Stadt Magdeburg beauftragt und befugt, als Verpächter in eigenem Namen und auf eigene Rechnung den vorliegenden Pachtvertrag abzuschließen. In Ausübung und Wahrnehmung des Rechtes zur gastronomischen Bewirtschaftung, bedient sich die MVGM eines erfahrenen Partners mit Gastronomie- bzw. Cateringunternehmen-Erfahrung. Durch dieses Cateringunternehmen erfolgt die gastronomische Versorgung zu Veranstaltungen jeglicher Art in allen Bereichen innerhalb des Objekts Stadthalle. Die gastronomische Betreuung der Veranstaltungsteilnehmer spielt eine wichtige Rolle für die Zufriedenheit der Kunden und Gäste. Die Qualität und Zuverlässigkeit der Leistungen des Caterers trägt daher maßgeblich zum Erfolg von Veranstaltungen in Stadthalle Magdeburg bei. Die Vertragspartner wollen mit Abschluss dieses Vertrages eine ordnungsgemäße und qualitativ überzeugende gastronomische Bewirtschaftung in der Stadthalle Magdeburg sicherstellen. Dafür erfordert die Art der Zusammenarbeit zwischen den beteiligten Parteien eine vertrauensvolle, faire und partnerschaftliche Zusammenarbeit. Die Parteien sind sich einig, dass die Qualität der Leistungen im Vordergrund steht und eine ziel- und lösungsorientierte Zusammenarbeit die Grundlage hierfür bildet.

title: J063--SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE - PARKING GATE SYSTEM REPLACEMENT, REMOTE MONITORING, PIV BADGE READER INTEGRATION AND SERVICE AGREEMENT FOR THE WASHINGTON DC VAMC
description: SUMMARY The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 5, is issuing this Sources Sought Notice to identify vendors that are interested in and capable of providing the required services. The Washington DC VA Medical Center requires a contractor to provide a Parking Gate System Replacement, Remote Monitoring, PIV Badge Reader Integration and 5 year Service Agreement for the facility. Interested vendors should review the Statement of Work (SOW) to determine the specific services required. NCO 5 is seeking responses from firms that are interested in this procurement and possess the resources, capabilities, and qualifications necessary to perform these services. Anticipated NAICS CODE 561621 Security Systems Services (except Locksmiths), PSC CODE J063 Please submit your capabilities statement and provide responses to all questions listed below. SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE: 36C24527Q0083 1. Business name (including Unique Entity ID (SAM.gov) 2. Business type, socio-economic status (e.g., Veteran-Owned, Woman-Owned, Disadvantaged Small Business, 8(a), etc.), and 3. Person of contact (including telephone number & email address). 4. Capability statement and summary of previous experience providing these types of services for the Veterans Health Administration or other similar facilities. 5. Available contract vehicles (GSA FSS, etc.) for use by Department of VA (including applicable NAICS) 6. Brief Summary of categories of services that your company can/cannot provide. 7. Certification(s) / Licenses for meeting the local requirements to provide these services at the DC VAMC (if applicable) 8. Confirmation that your organization has the capability and expertise to meet the performance requirements while complying with applicable limitations in subcontracting by responding to the questions below with your response: a. Do you intend to self-perform this effort? b. If you are located outside the immediate area, how will you self-perform? c. Or do you intend to subcontract work under this contract? If you intend to subcontract work under this contract, how will you ensure compliance with the limitations on subcontracting? Response Instructions: Respond to this Notice 36C24527Q0083 by 12-15-2026 @ 10 AM ET. Send all responses to Billie.Pratt@va.gov Subject line on email: 36C24527Q0083 Sources Sought Notice | Company Name STATEMENT OF WORK Parking Gate System Replacement, Remote Monitoring, PIV Badge Reader Integration and Service Agreement Department of Veterans Affairs | Washington DC VA Medical Center 50 Irving Street NW, Washington, DC 20422 Draft dated October 27, 2026 1. BACKGROUND The Washington DC VA Medical Center (VAMC) controls vehicle access to its parking areas, service drives and the separated Fisher House locations through nineteen (19) automated gates: eighteen (18) barrier-arm gates and one (1) slide gate at Utility Building 8. The existing gate operators are at end of service life, depend on in-ground loop detectors in deteriorated asphalt, and experience frequent vehicle strikes and extended downtime. The existing card readers at the gates are not uniformly capable of reading Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials, and VA Police Service cannot centrally manage parking-area access. VA requires (a) replacement of the gate operating equipment with commercial, high-duty equipment and above-ground vehicle detection, (b) remote status monitoring, event cameras and remote gate control for authorized VA personnel, (c) all-new PIV badge readers at each gate, furnished and installed by Johnson Controls, Inc. (JCI) as a subcontractor to the prime, and integrated into the VA Police Service physical access control system (PACS) so VA Police can control access to the facility parking areas, and (d) a firm-fixed-price service agreement covering a base year plus four (4) one-year option periods. 2. SCOPE OF WORK The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, equipment, materials, tools, transportation, subscriptions, and subcontracted services (including the mandatory JCI subcontract in Section 5) necessary to remove the existing gate equipment and furnish, install, test, commission, warrant, monitor, and maintain a complete and operational parking gate and access control system at the 19 gate locations, in accordance with this SOW, manufacturer requirements, and the referenced codes and standards. Equipment brand names in this SOW, other than the JCI/PACS requirement in Section 5, are "or equal." 3. LOCATIONS AND EXISTING CONDITIONS Item Location / Type Quantity Notes 1 Barrier-arm gates (standard duty, 12 14 ft arm) 17 Parking lots and service drives; includes separated Fisher House locations. 2 Barrier-arm gate (long arm, approx. 20 ft) 1 Heavy-duty operator; status reporting appropriate to hardware. 3 Slide gate Utility Building 8 1 Reuse existing gate panel; convert from top track to bottom steel cantilever track. 4 Lots 3B and 4B Gates as installed (verify) Relocatable (forklift-movable) foundations and flexible wiring for planned two-way operation. Total gate locations 19 Contractor shall verify all locations and conditions during the mandatory site visit. Existing 120 VAC power is available at each gate location. Any electrical deficiency found during the site survey shall be reported in writing to the COR before installation; correction of pre-existing deficiencies will be addressed by modification if outside this scope. 4. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS GATE SYSTEM 4.1 Removal and Disposal Remove existing operators, arms, controls, and abandoned detectors at all 19 locations; legally dispose of all removed material off VA property (batteries recycled per EPA/DC regulations). Clean and prepare concrete pads. Removal and replacement shall be sequenced so that no parking area loses all vehicle access at once without a VA Police-approved traffic plan. 4.2 Barrier Gate Operators Commercial/industrial, high-cycle (continuous-duty) DC barrier operators listed to UL 325 and installed per ASTM F2200 where applicable. Integral or supplemental battery backup at every location. Behavior on loss of primary power (fail-open or fail-secure) shall be programmable per location and set as directed in writing by the Chief, VA Police Service. LED-illuminated arms (high-visibility), breakaway/swing-away arm flanges at standard-arm locations, and arm-displacement (arm-missing) contacts wired to the monitoring system. Above-ground radar ("virtual loop") vehicle detection configured for safety, arming, reset and free-exit functions as required per lane; no reliance on in-pavement loops at barrier locations. One (1) spare barrier operator, identical to the installed standard model, delivered to VA as Government property. 4.3 Slide Gate Utility Building 8 Convert the existing gate panel from top (aluminum) track to bottom steel cantilever track with carriages, guide rollers and fabrication as required. Furnish and install a high-traffic commercial DC slide gate operator rated for the gate weight/length, with battery backup, monitored contact edges, wireless edge transmitter, and photo-eye entrapment protection meeting UL 325 Type B1/B2 requirements; reconnect to existing loop detectors where serviceable. 4.4 Relocatable Foundations Lots 3B and 4B Provide relocatable, forklift-movable operator foundations and flexible wiring arrangements so the Contractor or VA can relocate operators for large deliveries or lot reconfiguration. Contractors and subsontractors have the option to conduct an on-site visit to determine the best approach for Southeastern Power project. title: Z2DA--666-27-102 Lightning Protection Update B71N
description: The purpose of this amendment 0001 is as follows: To extend due for proposals from November 27, 2026, to December 15, 2026, before 10:00 AM MT. All offers please email them to Elia L Ruiz Manzo at Elia-Laritza.Ruiz-Manzo@va.gov. To post site visit attendance sheet and agenda. All other items and conditions remain the same. A.1 List of Attachments See attached document: S04-Pre Construction Site Visit attendance. See attached document: S04 - Site Visit Meeting Doc. --------------------------------------------------------- GENERAL: Introduction: An inspection for current code compliance of the lightning Protection System on Building 71N has been conducted and found the system needs upgrades and repairs to meet current NFPA 780 and UL96A standards. The Sheridan VA Medical Center needs the services of a qualified contractor to perform the needed lightning protection upgrades to the main hospital building 71N. Located on the Sheridan Wyoming Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) campus, at 1898 Fort Road, Sheridan, Wyoming 82801. Statement of Work: Specifics a. Existing Conditions The existing lightning protection system (LPS) for Building 71N was installed in 1989 during the building s original construction. Overall, the system remains in fair condition, though it requires repair because several air terminals have become detached from their adhesive bonds to the roof surface. Air terminals are present at all high points of the structure, and all roof-mounted equipment and appurtenances are properly grounded. A main grounding bus connects the communication systems and possibly the electrical distribution system to the primary service ground. The specific location where the grounding system bonds together the structural steel, electrical system, lightning protection components, and plumbing to create an equipotential ground could not be identified during the assessment. A continuous grounding loop encircles Buildings 9, 71, and 71N, with all roof air terminals and down conductors tied into this loop. Down conductors descend to the loop at the corners of each of these buildings. Each air terminal has at least two separate grounding paths, satisfying current code requirements. No Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices were observed in the system. The lower 8 feet of the ground down conductors are encased in PVC electrical conduit for protection. New Construction Recent construction has added large equipment and a screen wall to the roof, which now obstructs and interferes with the original positioning of the existing air terminals. This new equipment sits higher than the existing lightning protection system components, rendering the current air terminals ineffective at intercepting and safely directing lightning strikes to ground. Project Requirements To bring the existing lightning protection system (LPS) into compliance the following corrections are needed: Install Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices at the building s main service panel. Establish proper bonding by interconnecting all electrical systems, communication systems, piping, and structural steel at the service entrance to create an equipotential ground. Repair all roof air terminals that have detached or pulled away from their adhesive mounts on the roof surface. Install new air terminals at both ends of each screen wall, with additional terminals spaced at 20-foot intervals along the top of each wall, and at the highest point of the HVAC ductwork. Install an air terminal at each corner of the new HVAC equipment. Connect all newly installed air terminals to the existing LPS using #2 bare copper conductors. After these corrections have been completed, a qualified inspection is required to verify full compliance with NFPA 780 and UL 96A standards. Upon successful inspection, a Master Label Certificate should be issued for the lightning protection system. General: Construction project is to be completed within 120 calendar days from date of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractor shall provide all equipment, materials, supplies, tools, software, supervision, and labor required for this project, which may include, but is not limited to, demolition work, providing negative pressure environment for work, and providing all new equipment, utilities, and room finishes as indicated in the plans and this SOW per VA construction standards. Safety submittals shall be completed and approved prior to the commencement of on-site construction work. Material selection submittals shall be completed and approved prior to ordering of materials for the project. The building tenants not in the construction areas will remain at work in the buildings during this construction. Patients will remain on the floor in areas not under construction, so the contractor shall make patient safety, and infection control measures a priority. The contractor shall coordinate work locations and schedules with VA COR to minimize impact to building tenants. All electrical, carpentry, architectural, mechanical work, product design, project management, and other work needed on this project shall be provided by the Contractor. All required electrical work, low, medium, or high voltage, shall be installed and terminated by the Contractor. No wiring or cabling shall be abandoned in place. All piping, cabling, and wiring shall be labeled. All cabling and patch cabling shall match the VAMC s station-standard colors. The installation must, at a minimum, be in accordance with all applicable codes indicated in the Department of Veterans Affairs Design Manuals and VA .PUBLICATIONS (Master Construction Specifications, Construction Standards, National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), Underwriters Laboratory (UL), International Building Code IBC 2003, and National Electric Code (NEC) building codes and standards and the VA Information Security Handbook 6500.6, 6550.0 etc.). The Contractor shall read and be familiar with the most current editions of the applicable codes, standards, guides, and manuals. Sources can be accessed at the Office of Construction and Facilities Management s Technical Information Library (TIL) (http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL). Any penetrations through any floors, ceilings, or walls shall be fire caulked, or otherwise fire sealed, and shall be done in this contract to meet VA standards and NFPA standards. Contractor shall utilize the VAMC s station-standard fire stop products or approved equal product(s). The station-standard products are SpecSeal fire caulk product is SpecSeal SSS Intumescent Firestop Sealant; and, if needed, the SpecSeal Composite Sheet may be used in areas approved by the COR. The Contractor shall inquire of the COR if any existing equipment, fixtures, hardware, doors, frames, or any other property removed is desired to be retained by the VA for reuse elsewhere within the medical center, at the time of removal. If the VA desires to retain an item, the Contractor shall deliver it to a location designated by the COR. If the VA does not desire to retain an item, the Contractor shall dispose of it properly off-station. The new components installed shall be tested and commissioned, re-certified, and/or tested before VA acceptance. All testing parameters shall be provided by the Contractor with source references to the COR and 3rd-party reviewer before testing begins. Copies of all test reports must be provided to the COR. HVAC systems that have changes made to them as part of this project, beyond diffuser replacement, shall be tested and balanced by the Contractor. Any IT data cables installed or modified as part of this effort shall be tested after installation. Test methods and plans shall be coordinated with the COR. Any Med Gas systems modified as part of this effort shall be re-certified back to the closest shut-off in the system. The Contractor shall arrange for any required re-certification as part of this contract and shall provide plans and results to the COR for approval. Fire alarm

title: 6515--Patient Lifts and Slings for In Home Use
description: Patient Lifts & Slings for In Home Use This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 36C10G27R0002 is issued as a� request for proposal (RFP) for Patient Lifts and Slings (for in home use) as a uniform preferred product for Veterans, service members, and their families, who have earned through their military service to the United States. VHA accomplishes its mission by delivering patient-centered, personalized services that help Veterans readjust to civilian life and enhance their well-being. The Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) Veteran Health Administration (VHA), Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service (PSAS) has a need for Hydraulic Patient Lifts and Battery Powered Patient Lifts with Slings which are assistive devices that allows ability for caregivers to transfer Veterans between a bed, a chair or other similar resting places. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a supply source that will provide the contracted items to be utilized by Veterans Affairs Medical Centers (VAMCs). The objective is to ensure availability and consistency of products for nationwide usage and to obtain volume-based, standardized pricing. Standardization provides Veterans with high-quality continuity of healthcare and gives the VA concentrated buying power. This standardization initiative is in accordance with VHA Directive 1761.1. The Government seeks to establish an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract(s) with a period of performance of one (1) base year and four (4), one (1) year options. The requirement is solicited as a partial set aside for small business concerns for the Battery Powered Patient Lifts portion of the acquisition and Full and Open competition for the Hydraulic Patient Lifts portion of the acquisition. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the procurement of these items is 339113 with a small business size standard of 800 employees. Please identify your business size in your response based upon this standard. The government will only establish award(s) with the Offeror(s) that meets all requirements of the solicitation. The award(s) resulting from this solicitation will be made based on the best overall proposal that is determined to be the most beneficial to the Government (i.e., best value). Place of Performance: Multiple locations throughout the continental US, Hawaii and all US Territories; delivery location(s) will be defined per each order. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at� www.acquisition.gov. All vendors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database https://sam.gov. This acquisition is being conducted in accordance with the procedures in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services in conjunction with FAR Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation, FAR Part 16.504 Indefinite-quantity Contracts, and FAR Part 16.505 Ordering. Proposals must be submitted in accordance with the instructions provided under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.212-1 Instructions to Offerors Commercial Items. The proposal must be submitted no later than December 15, 2026, 12 PM EST unless this date is changed via a formal solicitation amendment. The contractor shall submit an electronic (email) copy of the proposal to both Noel Echevarria, Contract Specialist at Noel.Echevarria@va.gov and Brian Love, Contracting Officer at Brian.Love@va.gov. The Government is not responsible for confirming receipt. Any proposal received after the specified date and time will be unresponsive and shall receive no further consideration. In accordance with FAR 52.212-1(c), Offerors are responsible for submitting offers and any modifications or revisions to the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation. These e-mail addresses identified for the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer are the Government office designated in the solicitation as defined in FAR 52.212-1(c)(1) for timely receipt of proposals. Exceptions for late receipt of electronic submissions are specifically outlined in FAR 52.212-1(c)(2).

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) DDG 1000 Class Modernization: USS Michael Monsoor (DDG 1001) Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) Depot Modernization Period (DMP); Large Missile Vertical Launch System (LMVLS) Heavy Lift and Industrial Installation
description: 1.0 PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE PAE Maritime, on behalf of the dPAE Combatants/ DDG 1000 Class Program Office (PMS 500), is conducting market research to assess industry capabilities, engineering rigor, and shipyard infrastructure necessary to accomplish the industrial integration and installation of the Large Missile Vertical Launch System (LMVLS) aboard the USS Michael Monsoor (DDG 1001). The primary objective of this RFI is to evaluate prospective offerors' specific technical expertise, dry dock/pier-side heavy-lift capabilities, dimensional control methodologies, and integrated production scheduling to execute the installation of a pre-manufactured ~600-ton LMVLS module and associated Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) warfare alterations. The questions contained in Section 3.0 are specifically structured to allow industry respondents to demonstrate their understanding of the unique structural, spatial, lifting, and combat systems complexities associated with this depot modernization period. 2.0 TECHNICAL BASELINE & REQUIREMENT SUMMARY Key technical parameters within the DDG 1001 CPS DMP include: 2.1 Ship Particulars Vessel: USS Michael Monsoor (DDG 1001) Length Overall (LOA) / LBP: 186 m (610 ft) / 182.9 m (600 ft) Beam (Maximum): 24.6 m (80.7 ft) Draft (Navigational / DWL): 8.4 m (27.6 ft) / 7.0 m (23.0 ft) Hull Form & Superstructure: Wave-piercing tumblehome hull; steel hull structure with composite deckhouse; integrated power system (IPS). 2.2 LMVLS Pre-Manufactured Assembly Profile (GFM) The Government plans to deliver the LMVLS as Government-Furnished Material (GFM) as a fully out-fitted, pre-manufactured modular block. The industrial effort will require rigging, lifting, transferring, lowering, and setting the ~600-ton LMVLS module into the hull pocket within tight spatial and angular tolerances. Additional specifications include: Envelope Dimensions: Approximately 44� 7� Length � 20� 8� Width � 41� 1� Height. Total Lift Weight: Approximately 600 Long Tons (LT). Component Integration: Four (4) launch tubes housing Advanced Payload Modules (APMs) and All-Up Round Canisters (AUR-C), integral shock-isolation foundation assemblies, multi-level bulkheads (down through L5), decks, pre-installed outfitting, and weather deck / 01-level hatch structures. Installation Location: Forward Stack 1400 (reclaimed forward space following MT 61 AGS complete removal). 3.0 TECHNICAL CAPABILITY QUESTIONNAIRE Interested sources are requested to provide detailed technical narrative responses, supported by engineering calculations, facility specifications, past performance references, and risk mitigation methodologies, addressing each section below. Section A: Heavy Lift, Rigging & Facility Engineering Capabilities Lifting Infrastructure & Capacities: Detail your primary crane assets (gantry, floating, portal, or crawler) capable of hoisting and swinging a 600-ton (approx. 1,344,000 lbs) rigid modular assembly. Provide the specific crane load charts demonstrating rated capacity at the required operating radius and minimum hook height necessary to clear DDG 1001�s deck edge, bulwarks, and adjacent deckhouse structures (taking into account the 41� 1� module height plus lifting beam/spreader bar rigging height). If utilizing a floating crane for the LMVLS, confirm that the selected crane has the clearance to transit under any bridges necessary to arrive at your shipyard. Specify whether the 600-ton lift will be executed in dry dock or pier-side, and detail the structural load-bearing capacity (pounds per square foot / ground bearing pressure) of the quay wall, pier apron, or dry dock wing walls supporting the crane footprint during maximum outrigger or track loadings. Rigging, Stability & Tandem Operations: Describe your concept for the lift rigging assembly (spreader frames, equalizing grommets, dynamic load monitoring systems) to eliminate torsional deflection, racking, and localized stress concentrations on the pre-assembled LMVLS module during the pick. If a tandem or multi-crane lift is planned, provide your operational methodology for synchronous motion, hook travel rate synchronization, and emergency load re-distribution mitigation. Address environmental limits: What are your maximum allowable wind speed, wave/surge motion (if using floating derrick/crane barges), and tidal envelopes for executing this precision lift? Ship Mooring, Ballast & Hull Stability During Module Placement: DDG 1001 possesses a unique wave-piercing tumblehome form with strict naval architectural stability limitations. Describe your approach to calculate, model, and monitor ship list, trim, draft changes, and metacentric height during the removal of the forward AGS weight and subsequent setting of the 600-ton LMVLS module (whether afloat at a pier or during block contact in dry dock). Section B: Precision Alignment, Metrology & Structural Integration Dimensional Control & Metrology Framework: The LMVLS module must interface with existing ship structure, pre-established shock-attenuation foundations, and tight topside radar cross-section (RCS) deck tolerances. Describe your advanced metrology procedures (e.g., 3D laser scanning, photogrammetry, laser tracking) from initial ship condition surveying through pre-lift verification and final post-weld alignment. Section C: Industrial Coordination, Schedule Phasing & AIT Co-Existence Integration of Alteration Installation Teams (AIT) & System OEMs: Installation of the CPS LMVLS requires extensive concurrent work by Government labs and weapon system prime contractors (e.g., Raytheon, Lockheed Martin, NAVWAR). Detail your approach for managing space conflicts, shared lifting/crane services, security access controls for classified weapon compartments, and jurisdictional hand-offs between shipyard trades and specialized weapon installers. Subcontracting, Teaming & Industrial Workshare: If teaming or significant subcontracting (>20%) is required to satisfy heavy crane, precision metrology, or specialized welding capabilities, outline your proposed organizational hierarchy, prime contractor oversight model, and quality assurance audit procedures. If responding as a Small Business prime under FAR 52.219-14, explicitly demonstrate how your organization will perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing and direct industrial labor. Section D: Risk Assessment, Lessons Learned & Resource Management Critical Technical & Industrial Risks: Identify what your organization views as the top three (3) critical technical failure modes or schedule risks during the LMVLS module installation (e.g., crane unavailability, structural distortion exceeding cell launch tolerances, GFM delivery mismatches, dry dock schedule creep). For each identified risk, provide specific, mitigation strategies and fallback procedures. 4.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS & SUBMISSION GUIDELINES 4.1 Content & Page Limitations Cover Sheet: CAGE Code, SAM UEI, MSRA/ABR status, business size under NAICS 336611 (Ship Building and Repairing), primary technical and contracts POCs. Volume I (Technical Capability Narrative): Not to exceed five (5) pages, addressing all questions in Section 3.0. Volume II (Facilities, Equipment & Crane Load Charts): Not to exceed five (5) pages, containing facility schematics, dry dock certified dimensions, dock loading curves, and relevant crane radius/load capacity charts. 4.2 Marking of Proprietary Information Respondents must clearly mark and isolate any proprietary data, trade secrets, or commercial pricing/cost methodologies. The Government will handle properly marked data in accordance with applicable statutory regulations and protect it as Business Sensitive. 4.3 Inquiries & Submission Points of Contact Submissions shall be delivered electronically via DoD SAFE or secure email no later than the time and date specified in the official SAM.gov synopsis: Procuring Contracting Officer: Brian Romano, PAE M 025 (brian.c.romano.civ@us.navy.mil) Contract Specialist: James Thom

The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a supply source that will provide the contracted items to be utilized by Veterans Affairs Medical Centers (VAMCs). The objective is to ensure availability and consistency of products for nationwide usage and to obtain volume-based, standardized pricing. Standardization provides Veterans with high-quality continuity of healthcare and gives the VA concentrated buying power. This standardization initiative is in accordance with VHA Directive 1761.1. The Government seeks to establish an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract(s) with a period of performance of one (1) base year and four (4), one (1) year options. The requirement is solicited as a partial set aside for small business concerns for the Battery Powered Patient Lifts portion of the acquisition and Full and Open competition for the Hydraulic Patient Lifts portion of the acquisition. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the procurement of these items is 339113 with a small business size standard of 800 employees. Please identify your business size in your response based upon this standard. The government will only establish award(s) with the Offeror(s) that meets all requirements of the solicitation. The award(s) resulting from this solicitation will be made based on the best overall proposal that is determined to be the most beneficial to the Government (i.e., best value). Place of Performance: Multiple locations throughout the continental US, Hawaii and all US Territories; delivery location(s) will be defined per each order. description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT. The FAA is seeking interest in a Grounds Maintenance Service contract at Albuquerque ARTCC (ZAB), 8000 Louisiana Blvd. NE, Albuquerque, NM 87109. The SOW with photos is attached to this announcement. If interested please email Carey.Gonzalez@FAA.gov with a CC of Josh.Haker@FAA.gov. The email subject must include "ZAB Grounds Maintenance-Interested Vendor" along with your company's capability statement and the following: Company Name: Company POC: Company Phone: Company Email: Company UEI: Weed control and groundskeeping services in Albuquerque, NM typically involve a variety of tasks aimed at maintaining the health, appearance, and functionality of outdoor spaces, whether they are residential, commercial, or public areas. These services can include: Weed Control: This involves the removal and prevention of unwanted plants and weeds that can affect the health of desired plants and the aesthetics of the landscape. Services may include manual removal, chemical treatments, and organic solutions tailored to the specific needs of the area. Lawn Care: Regular mowing, edging, aeration, fertilization, and reseeding are part of lawn care services to ensure a lush and healthy lawn. Providers often focus on using practices suitable for Albuquerque�s climate, including drought-resistant strategies. Landscaping: Design and maintenance of gardens and outdoor spaces, including planting flowers, shrubs, and trees that are suitable for the local climate. Landscaping might also include hardscaping elements such as patios, walkways, and irrigation systems. Tree and Shrub Care: Trimming, pruning, and health assessments for trees and shrubs are important to prevent disease, encourage growth, and maintain safety. Irrigation Systems: Installation and maintenance of irrigation systems to ensure efficient water use, crucial in Albuquerque�s arid environment. This might include drip systems or smart irrigation technologies. Seasonal Cleanups: Removal of leaves, debris, and other waste, particularly during fall and spring, to maintain a neat appearance and prevent plant disease. Pest Control: Management of pests that can damage plants and lawns, using environmentally friendly methods where possible. Groundskeeping for Commercial Properties: Enhanced services that may include parking lot maintenance, exterior cleaning, and snow removal in winter months. Providers in Albuquerque may offer customized plans based on the unique requirements of the property and the preferences of the property owner. Additionally, they typically emphasize sustainable practices to cope with the region's water scarcity and environmental concerns.

title: National Veterans Sports Programs & Special Events National Veterans Golden Age Games (NVGAG) National Veterans Creative Arts Festival (NVCAF) Transportation
description: This Performance Work Statement (PWS) defines the requirements for transportation services under an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. The contract supports two national?level Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) programs: � The National Veterans Golden Age Games (NVGAG), including annual site visits and event transportation during the ordering period. � The National Veterans Creative Arts Festival (NVCAF) for designated event years. This IDIQ provides a unified scope of transportation services required to support recurring national VA events. Each task order will define the event year, schedule, required vehicle quantities, routing requirements, and operational details. Except where a minimum is stated, passenger counts and quantities in this PWS are planning figures; each task order will state the firm requirements. 1.1 National Veterans Golden Age Games (NVGAG) NVGAG is a national senior adaptive rehabilitation program promoting fitness, independence, and quality of life for older Veterans. It features multi?event athletic competitions and recreational activities for Veterans with varying levels of physical ability. NVGAG also serves as a qualifying event for participation in the National Senior Games. 1.2 National Veterans Creative Arts Festival (NVCAF) The National Veterans Creative Arts Festival empowers Veterans to improve their mental and physical health through therapeutic creative arts experiences. The event reinforces the VA�s commitment to whole health, recovery-oriented care, and Veteran-centered services by celebrating resilience, achievement, and personal growth. Showcasing the intersection of artistry and healing, the event features National Veteran medalists invited for their artistic achievements and therapeutic use of the arts.

Please refer to the attachments section to access the updated documents. ________________________________________________________________________ Description The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service, Capital Projects Contracting Division, is pleased to announce the issuance of a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a highly qualified Contractor who can provide Construction Services to perform a Seismic Retrofit at the Clemente Ruiz Nazario U.S. Courthouse (Nazario Courthouse) located at 150 Carlos Chardon Avenue in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Nazario Courthouse will remain fully operational throughout the duration of the Seismic Retrofit. To ensure minimal disruption to Government operations, the work will predominantly be executed after business hours. The selected General Contractor will be required to ensure full compliance with the Government�s requirements for access and security. Additionally, the General Contractor will be required to complete this project in accordance with the construction drawings and specifications that will be issued for this project. Contract Type: The contract type for this procurement will be Firm-Fixed price. The line item schedule will include a lump sum item for the Base and Options. Price: The total magnitude of this project at award is between $40,000,000 and $50,000,000. Selection and Schedule: The General Contractor will be selected through a procurement method developed in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation (Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) and FAR 36 Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-36). The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Evaluation process. During Phase I, prospective firms must submit technical qualifications detailing their experience with comparable efforts and previous records of past-performance. In Phase II, selected General Contractors shall demonstrate their operational strategy and planned subcontracting framework. Evaluation of Phase II technical submissions will be conducted in full before the Government reviews the price proposal. GSA anticipates award of a contract for these services in August 2027. The period of performance for the proposed contract will be for approximately forty six (46) months upon issuance of notice to proceed. NAICS: This procurement will be conducted under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 236220--Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Small Business size standard is an average annual sales and receipts for the past three (3) years that are equal to or less than $45,000,000. All offerors are required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (www.SAM.gov) at the time of offer submission, and shall continue to be registered until time of award, during performance, and through final payment of any contract. Interested offerors - See all attached solicitation file packages for full details. Some of the solicitation documents are Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). To access these documents your company must request access through www.sam.gov. Proposals for this Solicitation must be submitted via e-mail in portable document format (PDF). Proposals MUST BE RECEIVED NO LATER THAN stated due date and time in this solicitation. Inquiries concerning this solicitation must be routed to Contracting Officer Natalia Lugo-Vina at natalia.lugo-vinacruz.gsa.gov. Prospective offerors bear sole responsibility for tracking and retrieving the RFP alongside all associated modifications.

title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: UPDATE #1 � Amendment #0001 to the RFP was released on October 22, 2026. UPDATE #2 � Amendment #0002 to the RFP was released on October 26, 2026. UPDATE #3 - Amendment #0003 to the RFP was released on November 20, 2026. UPDATE #4 - Amendment #0004 to the RFP was released on November 24, 2026. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: UPDATE #1 � Amendment #0001 to the RFP was released on October 22, 2026. UPDATE #2 � Amendment #0002 to the RFP was released on October 26, 2026. UPDATE #3 - Amendment #0003 to the RFP was released on November 20, 2026. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

As part of market research, this Sources Sought notice is to determine whether an adequate number of qualified, interested vendors exist that can provide the required goods and services required. Additionally, USACE intends to surveil the market to determine the availability of qualified small business contractors to perform these services and to determine socioeconomic classifications (Small Business, HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses, Women Owned Small Businesses, etc.) associated with each. The shoe segments are a truncated pie shape with dimensions approximately 19.26 inches long, 23.72 inches wide (at OD), and 13.43 inches wide (at ID). The bearing shoes are 8 inches thick, including a babbitt layer of 0.13 inches. The scope of work consists of: Provide round-trip transportation of the thrust shoes between the project and refurbishment facility. Perform as-received inspections and document the condition for every shoe. Conduct pre-babbitt NDT (visual (VT) and liquid penetrant (PT)) and obtain Government acceptance. Remove old babbitt and prepare the shoes. Restore the steel backing / backside of the shoes. Re-babbitt the running surface of the shoes by pouring new babbitt. The new babbitt metal shall be new material conforming to ASTM B 23 Alloy 2. The tin used for tinning shall be 99 percent pure. Use of reclaimed metal will not be acceptable. Restore functional features and final geometry of the shoes. Perform final babbitt-bond NDT (ultrasonic test (UT) and liquid penetrant (PT)) of the shoes. Final inspection, reporting, and Government release of the shoes. Preserve and return the completed shoes.
